newsitem.title: UK: UK drug shares up on pre-budget safe-haven buying.
newsitem.headline: UK drug shares up on pre-budget safe-haven buying.

text.p: Shares in leading British pharmaceutical companies rallied on Monday on the back of strength in their American Depository Receipts (ADRs) and ahead of the government's budget on Wednesday.
The large multinational companies were being viewed as a safe-haven ahead of the budget from Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown, analysts and traders said.

SmithKline Beecham Plc traded 11.5p higher at 11.09 stg at 0904 GMT after hitting a year high of 11.15. Zeneca Group Plc also registered a new year high of 20.15-1/2 stg and then eased back to 19.99, up four.
"These stocks are seen as very safe, big international stocks," one analyst said. "People are moving toward safety."
Analysts were also pleasantly suprised with Zeneca and Smithkline Beecham during recent meetings and were likely to be upgrading their outlooks for the second half of the year, he said.

Glaxo lagged the other drug companies after Natwest cut its 1997 estimates for operating margins to 35.5 percent, market sources said. Natwest kept its "add" rating on the stock, which was up one penny at 12.39 stg.
Shares were already down from the year's high of 12.99 stg after analysts at BZW last week issued a cautious comment and recommended its clients to reduce their holdings.
"There is nothing bullish today except for the pharmaceuticals which were strong on the Street on Friday," a trader said.
The analyst said all three shares were "still fundamentally undervalued" which could fuel further gains through the budget.
